title: The Closed record shows the category's new name after a rename
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure AccountingHub is enabled for the organization and the test location has no QuickBooks Online connection.
  • Have a new No Charge category for this test, category A, mapped to an account.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A.
  • Have a new No Charge work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, category category A, closed.
custom_steps:
1. Open Administration > Service > Internal Work Orders.
  2. Rename category A.
  3. Open Accounting > Sales > Invoices.
  4. Open work order 1's record.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The categories page opens.

Step 2:

  • Category A shows its new name.

Step 3:

  • Work order 1's Closed record is listed.

Step 4:

  • Its summary shows the category's new name.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11758 (Story 1, Turn on Internal Work Orders, flag internal customers, manage categories), story SV-11765 (Story 8, AccountingHub, the closed work order and its parts cost)

  • S8-R1: “At Close, the hub receives the invoice event carrying the classification (Internal or No Charge), the category, the original work order and line and the original technician when set, the work order number and the asset, and keeps an invoice record with a status Closed (new in the hub), the badge, "No Charge" in place of a total, and no payment tabs. It posts no revenue, no receivable and no tax for it. The record's page (Accounting > Sales > Invoices) shows the header with the existing link to the work order in ShopView, a summary (number, customer, asset, classification, category, original work order when set, posting date, "No Charge", and the posted Parts cost and Shop supplies totals) and the journal entry section with the entries of S8-R2 and S8-R3; no lines (they are on the NO CHARGE document), no payment, credit memo or write-off tabs and no Void (Reopen is done in ShopView, Story 4).”
  • S1-R16: “A category has a stable key; renaming it keeps the history, the report filter and the mappings. Archiving a category in use keeps it on existing work orders, lines, documents and reports; it is no longer offered in any select. The default Internal category cannot be archived; changing the default moves nothing on existing customers. The green QuickBooks mark (the existing QuickBooks icon) is shown wherever a field maps to QuickBooks: the account columns and pickers of S1-R13 and S1-R14, the asset field of S1-R15 and the Settings hint of S1-R3. Archiving a category that is the stored default of customers or assets first shows "[n] internal customers and [m] assets use this category as their default. Their new work orders will use the next category in line." The stored value stays on the customer and the asset, shown as "[name] (archived)" with the hint "Archived. Pick an active category."; resolution for a new work order (S2-R1) skips archived categories: the asset's, else the customer's, else the default Internal category, the first active one wins. Restore puts everything back as it was.”

From: "Internal Work Orders technical implementation plan", 2026-10-28, last updated 2026-11-10 (revision 5, built on PRD v1.0), sources/TECH-PLAN-Internal-Work-Orders-upload-2026-11-12.md, read 12 Nov 2026

  • Tech plan line 4079 (TP-575): “snapshot at Close; read side prefers the current name”
